A rug pull is a scam in which the developers of a crypto project withdraw the funds or liquidity and abandon the project. A rug pull leaves investors holding tokens that have little or no value. A rug pull is used in forums and social media as an accusation or warning about fraudulent projects.

Not your keys, not your coins is a saying that warns holders that crypto kept on a third-party platform is not fully under their own control. Not your keys, not your coins describes the risk that the custodian may fail, freeze, or lose the assets. Not your keys, not your coins is used in the community to advise holding assets in self-custody.

Lambo is slang that refers to a Lamborghini and expresses the hope of large crypto gains. Lambo is used to describe speculative optimism about price rises. Lambo is often used humorously rather than as a direct warning about harm.

Burn crypto refers to permanently destroying tokens by sending them to an address from which they cannot be recovered. Burn crypto reduces the circulating supply of a token. I do not know the exact slang meaning of Burn crypto when used in warnings about risks and harms, so this description covers only the token-burning mechanism.

Exit liquidity describes the buyers who provide the demand that insiders need in order to sell their holdings. Exit liquidity is used to accuse a project's insiders of selling to later buyers. Exit liquidity warns that buyers who arrive late may be left holding assets that lose value.
